title: autotune: default batching/caching heuristics + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Defaults and tooling: 1) smarter autotune defaults for batching and caching to reduce p50/p95 token cost by ~12-18% on common RLHF-like workloads; 2) new quantization profile selector that prefers 4-bit profiles for compatible models with detailed fallback rules; 3) unit-economics CLI + console recommendations that surface expected cost delta for profile changes.
description: Motivation: We have several customer cohorts that manually tune batching, cache TTLs and quantization profiles to reduce per-token cost. This is error-prone and yields inconsistent unit economics across workloads. This change bundles three related improvements to automate sane defaults and give operators clear cost visibility. Changes in this PR: 1) runtime: introduce an autotune defaults module that computes initial batching window and continuous-batcher target size based on historical sequence-length distribution and latency SLO. The heuristic prefers slightly smaller batches for tail-latency sensitive routes and larger batches for throughput-oriented routes; TTL-based prefix caching is adjusted to be conservative for short-lived sessions. 2) quantization: add QuantProfileSelector that scores available quant profiles (4-bit, 8-bit, fp16) based on model compatibility, observed output-quality proxies, and expected speed/cost on current hardware; includes deterministic fallbacks and an opt-out tag for models that require higher precision. 3) unit-econ tooling: add a CLI subcommand `redwood uecon simulate` and backend endpoints that compute expected token-cost delta and expected latency impact for candidate configuration changes (batch size, cache TTL, quant profile). Also surfaces recommended config in the Console UI under Cost Recommendations. Implementation notes: - runtime/batching: added autotune/defaults.py and minor changes to scheduler/continuous_batcher.py to accept runtime hints (see files changed). Defaults are computed from a lightweight histogram maintained by the router for sequence lengths (hot-path optimized, probabilistic decay). - runtime/caching: updated policy.py to include a conservative default TTL calculation and to add a short-circuit for high-reuse prefixes. - optimize/autotune: new QuantProfileSelector, unit-econ estimator, and an async job to precompute recommendations for high-traffic routes. - tools/unit-econ: CLI changes and integration tests that simulate mixed trace workloads. - web/console: added CostRecommendations component and a small API adapter that fetches simulation results. Tests & CI: added unit tests for selector scoring (optimize/tests/test_quant_selector.py), integration tests for batching heuristic (runtime/tests/test_autotune_defaults.py), and e2e test for the CLI (tools/unit-econ/tests/test_cli_simulate.py). CI initially failed lint on a naming nit and a flaky test related to deterministic seeding; fixes were pushed in the second commit and CI passed. Backwards compat: Default behavior is gated behind a feature flag `autotune_defaults_v1` which is enabled for 20% of tenant traffic initially; quant selection will never override model-level `precision:required` metadata. Rollout plan: - Enable feature flag at 20% for 3 days, monitor unit-econ deltas and p95 latency. - Expand to 50% if cost savings without >5% p95 regression. - If regression seen, automatic rollback to previous defaults. Checklist: - [x] runtime heuristics implemented - [x] quant selector + fallbacks - [x] uecon simulator CLI + backend - [x] Console UI integration - [x] unit/integration/e2e tests - [x] feature-flag gated rollout - [x] docs updated (docs/optimize/autotune.md) Related work: ENG-1245 (autotune epic), ENG-1302 (quant profiles), ENG-1378 (unit-econ work). See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1245/autotune-defaults-design for rationale and benchmarks. Merge notes: squash-and-merge; migration steps included to backfill per-route histograms for the last 7 days using a cheap map-reduce job (optimize/scripts/backfill_route_histograms.py).
review_comments: Diego Martinez: Can you justify the 20% rollout cap? Suggest adding a probe to detect skewed workloads that don't benefit from batching.
Ava Chen: Added probe to the estimator and clarified rollout rationale in design doc; kept 20% conservative initial ramp.
Priya Rao: Quant selector scoring looks good but add a stronger guard for safety-critical models (e.g. those with production accuracy SLAs)
Ava Chen: Added model-level `precision:required` opt-out and test coverage. Also added logging when selector downgrades precision.
Samir Patel: CI failed on flaky test — saw seeding non-determinism. After fixing test seed in commit 5 CI is green.
Diego Martinez: Approved after addressing comments.
notes: This PR reduces expected token cost on typical chat workloads and provides tooling to make config changes observable in unit economics before rollout. Feature-gated rollout reduces blast radius.
